# Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL and Its Benchmarks

## Research question

An aggregate can silently count repeated entities, and benchmark gold can encode the same mistake. Deciding whether repetition is wrong also requires the intended counting grain.

## Method

Uses sqlglot scopes and instance-level SQL probes to expose repeated rows, then LLM review to distinguish distorted from intended gold. Agent evidence adds measure grain, identifier repetition, NULL-aware dependencies and required-key scoping to ordinary dependency profiles.

## Evaluation

Audits BIRD and constructs 486 reviewed BIRD-FanOut questions plus 59 synthetic GrainTraps questions. Eight models compare seven evidence arms. Main runs expose reference-query tables; 183 distorted BIRD-train questions are held out from evidence design, while all GrainTraps questions are in-sample.

## What the results support

Grain-aware evidence reduces measured fan-out errors beyond statistics on the selected BIRD cases, including under two judge-free metrics. General accuracy gains are smaller and unestablished on held-out cases. Prompting models to check data increases checking without demonstrating fewer grain errors.

## Limits and qualifications

No human labeled or checked the benchmark data. Shared LLM judges, post-run gold review and metric selection, strong-model screening, outcome-selected design cases, different run days and bundled evidence additions constrain inference. The audit measures repetition rather than intent, and may flag correct intended counting.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides adjacent data-grounded verification and benchmark-quality tools for underspecified aggregation semantics. It neither proves full SQL correctness nor evaluates clarification, refusal or intrinsic database unanswerability.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Claim or inference examined | Original evidence | Location | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The audit establishes that 4.2% of BIRD gold is objectively wrong. | The reported 4.2% is 64 LLM-labeled distorted questions among 1,534 June 2024 dev questions, distinct from the 82 definite flags. The train 6.2% figure counts flags rather than adjudicated distorted questions. The paper states that no person labeled or checked any data. | Section 4/Figures4–6, pp.4–5; Section7 limitations, p.12 | Report an audit-and-LLM-label estimate for that BIRD release, not a human-adjudicated error rate for every BIRD version or benchmark. |
| Grain-aware evidence improves general Text-to-SQL accuracy by the headline error reduction. | The 18.4% to 13.1–13.6% figures concern exact-plus-judged fan-out errors on 229 selected distorted train questions. Against statistics, held-out fan-out decreases 2.7–2.9 points; judge-free metrics support the direction. Held-out accuracy gains are not significant, and the 183-question holdout is the complement of an outcome-selected 46-question design set. | Sections 5.2–6.3/Table 2/Figure 10, pp.7–10; Appendix E/Tables 10–11, p.17 | Supports reduction of a targeted error mode under the tested setup. Do not equate it with overall accuracy, random-split generalization or independent human-label validation. |
| A definite fan-out flag proves semantic error regardless of intent. | Section 4 uses that strong wording, but Proposition 2.1 assumes the requested measure grain. Section 6.7 explicitly says the audit cannot judge intent and flags 53% of correct answers on intended-repetition questions. It also flags AVG conservatively when repetitions are uniform. | Proposition 2.1/Section 2.2, pp.2–3; Section 4, p.4; Section 6.7, p.11 | Treat flag names as operational repetition diagnostics, not sound certificates of question–SQL mismatch. Whether repeated rows should count remains a semantic decision. |
| Independent BIRD revision verifies the audit’s complete precision and recall. | Answer changes occur in 36/82 definite-flag questions versus 217/1,397 unflagged questions; 55 weaker flags are set aside. The 32/36 detected fan-out fixes use LLM judgments of revision meaning, and missed-fix search only examines changes adding DISTINCT. | Section 4/Figure 6, p.5 | Provides corroborating enrichment in an independently revised release, not exhaustive detection performance or proof that every changed answer was a fan-out correction. |
